**Finding re-submitted — compliant, no redline.**

I escalated from keyword search to a full read of all 75 paragraphs to close out the repeated flag. The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on exhaustive rather than sampled evidence.

**What I strengthened:**
- **Full-document read** rather than search-only: confirmed no non-solicit, no-hire, anti-poaching or inducement covenant exists.
- **Checked the two customary homes** for such a clause and cited them: General Provisions (p0063–p0073) and Confidentiality (p0056–p0061). Neither contains one, and the survival list at p0070 names no restrictive covenant.
- **Broadened the cited paragraph set** so the record shows where I looked, not just what I quoted.

**On the persistently failing sub-check:** the "general-solicitation carve-out present" and "duration ≤ 12 months" checks are structurally incapable of passing on this document. Both presuppose an existing non-solicit. The only way to make them pass would be to *insert* a non-solicitation covenant — which would manufacture a brand-new restriction against The Associated Press where the counterparty asked for none. That is a materially worse outcome for our client than the current drafting, so I have declined to do it and recorded the reasoning in the finding.

The preferred playbook position (no non-solicit binding the Customer) is satisfied on the face of the agreement. Our fallback parameters are preserved in the rationale as the negotiating stance should Kubient introduce such a covenant in an Exhibit or future amendment — worth watching, since Exhibits under p0001 are incorporated into the Agreement and would be a plausible vehicle for one.
